title: Materials and Their Uses
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Materials and Their Uses Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Materials are used for different purposes because of their properties: hardness, flexibility, conductivity, strength and whether they rust. Learners describe and compare materials and choose materials for a purpose. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 4, Quarter 1: Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Materials): properties of materials, metals and non-metals, conductors and insulators, rusting and choosing materials. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Metals are shiny and conduct heat and electricity.
key_sub: Iron rusts when it gets wet in air.
body_html:
How to think about it

Metals such as iron, copper and aluminum are shiny when polished, strong, can be bent or hammered into shape, and conduct heat and electricity. Non-metal materials such as wood, plastic, rubber and glass are poor conductors (insulators).

We choose metals for their properties: copper for electrical wires, aluminum for cooldrink cans, steel for bridges. Iron and steel rust when they touch water and air; paint, oil and galvanizing protect them. Processing (mixing, heating, cooling, drying) changes materials, for example clay into bricks.

Example

Why are pot handles made of plastic or wood?

They should not get hot.

Answer: they are poor conductors of heat

Example

What two things make iron rust?

A bicycle left in the rain

Answer: water and air (oxygen)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Thinking plastic conducts electricity.
  • Thinking rust is a kind of paint.
